 Rajasthan: Winter intensifies as Fatehpur touches minimum temperature of season at 5.7 degrees Celsius
 By: Sunita Sarkar 
 Date:
 November 19, 2026 
 Winter conditions are gradually intensifying across Rajasthan, with temperatures dropping in several parts of the state, particularly in the Shekhawati region. Night temperatures have fallen significantly, bringing colder conditions during late-night and early-morning hours.
 According to the Meteorological Centre, Jaipur, minimum temperatures in the Shekhawati region are currently ranging between 6 degrees Celsius and 10 degrees Celsius, while most other parts of Rajasthan are recording minimum temperatures between 10 degrees Celsius and 16 degrees Celsius.
 During the past 24 hours, Fatehpur in Sikar district recorded the lowest minimum temperature in the state at 5.7 degrees Celsius.
 The weather department has forecast predominantly dry weather across most parts of Rajasthan over the next seven days, with no significant change in temperatures expected.
 However, under the influence of a weak western disturbance, partly cloudy conditions may develop over some parts of eastern Rajasthan on November 21 and 22.
 Weather experts said that skies are likely to remain clear across the state for the next three days. Minimum temperatures may fall further during this period, increasing the intensity of winter in the Shekhawati region and parts of the Bikaner division.
 Meanwhile, some changes in weather conditions may be witnessed in the Kota division next week. Fatehpur, near Sikar, experienced one of the coldest nights on Wednesday, with the minimum temperature recorded at 8 degrees Celsius.
 Several other cities also witnessed chilly night conditions. The hill station of Mount Abu recorded a minimum temperature of 10.7 degrees Celsius, while Alwar registered 10.2 degrees Celsius.
 The minimum temperature in Churu stood at 10.9 degrees Celsius, followed by Nagaur at 11 degrees Celsius, Karauli at 11.7 degrees Celsius and Sirohi at 11.9 degrees Celsius.
 According to the weather department, dry conditions are expected to continue across most parts of Rajasthan in the coming days. With night-time temperatures likely to decline further in some regions, residents may experience increased cold during early mornings and late nights.
